checkpoint_progress.step_4_obstacle_stop: FAILED (real finding, not yet resolved). Held a box ~15cm in front of the head. Robot repeatedly stopped-and-tried-again (flicker) rather than staying stopped, and DID make physical contact and push the box forward at least once. Root cause identified: autonomy/behavior.py's decide() (line 10-14) is a stateless single-threshold check (BLOCKED if distance<20cm else CLEAR) with no hysteresis/debounce, so a single noisy echo reading just above 20cm reads as CLEAR and triggers a step. settings.py already defines RESUME_THRESHOLD_CM=35.0 'D-06, hysteresis resume gate' but it is NEVER referenced anywhere in behavior.py — dead config. This is exactly the phase's own pre-identified 'Pitfall 2' (oscillation/hysteresis, see .planning/research/PITFALLS.md and 01-CONTEXT.md D-06), which the 01-01-PLAN.md itself explicitly scoped OUT of this plan and into plan 01-03 ('plan 03 replaces this with the three-state hysteresis machine', 01-01-PLAN.md line 201). So the code matches plan 01-01's spec exactly as written — but CLAUDE.md's stated non-negotiable core value is 'the hexapod can move around on its own without crashing into things, pets, or kids', and actual contact occurred. This is a genuine tension between the phase plan's sequencing and the project's safety bar. NOT YET RESOLVED — see pending_decision below.

root_cause_found_2026_08_08.summary: Ran autonomy/perception.py's standalone self-test (python3 -m autonomy.perception, hardware isolated from all gait/decision logic) with NOTHING in front of the sensor. Readings flickered almost randomly between None and 300.0 (the max_distance clamp value) with only one stray plausible reading (58.4) in ~100 samples over ~20s. This means the raw signal itself is garbage, not just noisy-near-threshold — no hysteresis value can fix a decision built on corrupted input.
root_cause_found_2026_08_08.confirmed_mechanism: Inspected gpiozero source directly (site-packages, this Pi's installed version). gpiozero.DistanceSensor.__init__ (input_devices.py:504-ish, called via Ultrasonic() in Code/Server/ultrasonic.py) unconditionally calls self._queue.start() — a GPIOQueue(GPIOThread) background thread that loops calling self._read() every sample_wait=0.06s (60ms) FOREVER, to feed the smoothed .distance property (used by the pre-existing CMD_SONIC teleop command, server.py:197-198 -> ultrasonic_sensor.get_distance()). SEPARATELY, autonomy/perception.py's SensorHub._poll_loop() ALSO calls self._ultrasonic.sensor._read() directly on its own 100ms cadence (SENSOR_POLL_HZ=10). Two threads calling the same instance's _read() (which fires a physical trigger pulse and waits on a shared Event for the echo) on uncoordinated schedules corrupts nearly every reading: leftover echo-pin-high state from one ping collides with the next thread's trigger, producing None (echo-pin-already-high or no-echo-received warnings) or bogus timing that computes as/clamps to max_distance (300.0 = 1.0 * 3.0m * 100).
root_cause_found_2026_08_08.why_hysteresis_didnt_help: The hysteresis fix (ff87cda) is still correct and should be kept, but it cannot compensate for an input signal that is essentially random noise between None and max-clamp — the real distance was almost never being measured at all, regardless of what threshold logic sits on top.
root_cause_found_2026_08_08.why_not_just_kill_gpiozeros_thread: Stopping gpiozero's internal GPIOQueue thread (sensor.sensor._queue.stop()) would silence the dual-poller race, but CMD_SONIC's existing get_distance()/.distance property depends on that same thread staying alive to keep the smoothed value fresh — killing it would silently freeze/break that already-shipped manual-teleop feature. Not an acceptable fix.
root_cause_found_2026_08_08.correct_fix_direction: Do not run a second independent polling thread in SensorHub at all. Instead, passively capture each reading as a side effect of gpiozero's OWN existing thread's calls to _read() (subclass DistanceSensor or wrap/monkeypatch the bound _read method on the existing Ultrasonic().sensor instance to also stash (value, monotonic_time) into a spot SensorHub.latest() reads from) so there is only ever ONE caller touching the physical trigger/echo pins. This preserves CMD_SONIC's existing behavior untouched (gpiozero's queue keeps running exactly as before) while giving SensorHub honest, uncorrupted, un-averaged visibility into every raw sample including Nones, with no contention.
root_cause_found_2026_08_08.user_directive: User asked whether to test hardware vs code first (good instinct) — this investigation is the result. Fix-it-now precedent already established from the earlier hysteresis decision; proceeding directly to spawn a continuation executor for this fix too unless the user says otherwise.
